This report recommends adding $1.65 million to the water conservation capital project for the spray pads improvement initiative.
Financing through a green loan is proposed with repayment planned over 10 years through annual water savings.
Spray pads provide safe and fun opportunities for the community to cool off during the summer months.
When implemented, the work will support the city's extreme heat emergency response plan by providing needed cooling amenities and public access to drinking water.
This spray pad improvements scope of work involves replacing existing water notal nozzles with low flow fixtures.
Controllers are planned for all 23 spray pad locations, which will allow remote adjustments to sequencing patterns and schedule changes to respond to extreme heat events.
Conservation of water in the spray pad features will help to increase resiliency in the water and wastewater treatment system and result in more efficient system operations.
The projects scope also includes climate adaptation improvements such as adding shade structures,
testing stations and water fountains at six sites to provide the public with opportunities to cool off and access drinking water.

The information report in front of you identifies increasing risk to our communities food security and proposes the preparation of a food action plan.
It outlines federal and municipal status on food security and summarizes the approach in other municipalities as well as in Saskatoon.
To progress the development of a food action plan principles are included which would guide the definition of the city's role in this area.
Welcome would be an action based implementation plan consisting of city led initiatives which would be developed by engaging with groups in the community and coordinating with their work next please.
As you're aware food security has become an important topic in Saskatoon and across the country.
It is having an impact on many people in our community in Saskatoon food bank usage has significantly increased including for those who are employed.
The food bank emergency food hamper program has increased 28% since last year and by almost 50% since 2019.

While emergency food services are being accessed more than ever at the same time research estimates that 58% of all food produced in Canada is lost or wasted of which 32% is avoidable and could be redirected.

This demonstrates how unaddressed gaps in the food system can exacerbate existing issues with food waste access and distribution but also that with proper planning and resources opportunities exist to improve how our food system functions from seed to table to soil next please.

Over the years the city has made progress to integrate food into its strategic documents food system work is identified in the official community plan as well as prioritized in the green pathways implementation plan next.

The city does not currently have a comprehensive plan which guides food related work and no department has been identified as leading and coordinating food security or food system work for the organization.
Individual initiatives, however, which focus on food production and food waste diversion have progressed.

In the community there are several organizations focused on food insecurity, education, gardening and food production local academic institutions offer programs and research focused on food and nutrition.
A growing number of businesses offer local, sustainable, healthy, cultural and or affordable food options next.

While addressing food resiliency requires efforts by several sectors, municipalities are often well positioned to address their localized food context and be responsive in the face of the food system disruptions.
Municipalities can also play a key role in coordinating efforts internally between departments and connect as a connector for activities being led by the community.
There are 64 municipalities across Canada that are addressing food security through planning documents and dedicated efforts next please.
Solidifying our municipal roles and responsibilities and how these translate into concrete actions could help address food insecurity risks in our community.
Specifically, a food action plan would help us in part to create a roadmap of city-led initiatives to guide our actions and decision making.
It could help us to coordinate or enhance existing work addressing emerging needs and potentially identify new initiatives.
We could be addressing gaps in our processes, programming policies and resources and lastly it can help to identify areas for improvement and leadership to enable action and remove barriers.
Creating a resilient food system, creating a resilient food system is multifaceted and it requires effort in several areas such as improving the accessibility availability and acceptability of food.
Applying a reconciliation equity diversity and inclusion lens to the work including how to support access to culturally appropriate foods.
Identifying ways to support businesses and economic development through food production, tourism, etc.
Improving community and community safety and well-being by, for example, addressing and preparing for food access emergencies.
Supporting recreation and leisure activities that promote quality of life through stewardship activities and the growing and sharing of food.
This next step in creating a food action plan involves submitting a business plan option for the reserve for capital expenditures funding consideration of the 2025 budget.
